academic.title: Understanding the CE and BCE Dating System: The Absence of Year Zero and Its Historical Implications
academic.abstract: This paper clarifies the Common Era (CE) and Before Common Era (BCE) system, emphasizing the historical absence of year zero, its mathematical and chronological implications, and differences from astronomical year numbering. Clear examples and visual timelines support accurate historical reasoning.

advaita_vedanta.heading: Advaita Vedanta and Adi Shankara (8th century CE)
advaita_vedanta.influence: Advaita Vedanta has deeply influenced Indian spirituality, literature, and interfaith dialogue. Its teachings continue to inspire seekers worldwide.
key_concepts: Brahman is the only reality; the world is ultimately illusory (maya).
Atman (Self) is not different from Brahman.
Ignorance (avidya) causes bondage; knowledge leads to liberation.
Emphasizes scriptural study, reasoning, and meditation.
advaita_vedanta.summary: Advaita Vedanta is a major school of Indian philosophy that teaches non-dualism—the essential oneness of the individual soul (Atman) and the Supreme Reality (Brahman). Adi Shankara (c. 788–820 CE) revitalized Advaita, traveling across India to debate, teach, and establish monastic centers (mathas). His commentaries on the Upanishads, Bhagavad Gita, and Brahma Sutras remain foundational. Advaita emphasizes that liberation (moksha) is attained through knowledge (jnana) of the true Self, transcending all distinctions.

timeline.notes: Established four mathas in India; spread Advaita philosophy.

intro.summary: CE (Common Era) and BCE (Before Common Era) are neutral date labels using the same year numbering as AD and BC. There is no year zero in historical dating; 1 BCE transitions directly to 1 CE.
